results.title: N. Korean FM slams G7 nations' call for denuclearization, says its nuclear pursuit remains 'steadfast'
results.content: North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui denounced Thursday a joint call from major countries for denuclearization of the regime, saying its commitment to nuclear buildup remains "steadfast." Choe made the remarks in a commentary released by state media, after the Group of Seven (G7) advanced nations issued a joint statement following their foreign ministers' meeting in Paris earlier this week. The joint statement strongly condemned the North's illicit nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs, reaffirming their commitment to realizing the "complete denuclearization" of North Korea in accordance with U.N. Security Council (UNSC) resolutions. The UNSC resolutions ban Pyongyang from developing those weapons. results.title: Kim Yoon-seok, Koo Kyo-hwan deliver gripping tension in snowy thriller 'White Blast'
results.content: Actors Kim Yoon-seok and Koo Kyo-hwan reunite on screen for the first time in five years in "White Blast," delivering a sharp, intense mystery thriller where psychological tension and dark humor collide inside a snowbound rural train station. Directed by Hong Eui-jeong and Park Sun-woo, the upcoming movie is considered one of the most anticipated Korean releases this winter. With a compact 89-minute runtime, the movie relies heavily on the dynamic between its two lead actors. Set against the heavy snowfall in mountainous Gangwon Province, the story follows Gap-soo (Kim), a veteran stationmaster just one day away from retirement, and Hyeon-taek (Koo), his newly assigned successor. When a mysterious corpse turns up at the isolated station during a severe snowstorm, the two men are drawn into a tense psychological battle. results.title: Seoul vows continued Ukraine aid despite POW row
results.content: South Korea's foreign ministry said Thursday it would maintain its commitment to supporting Ukraine despite a diplomatic dispute over Kyiv's transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul. "As a responsible member of the international community, we will continue to maintain our principled position on providing assistance to Ukraine," a foreign ministry official told AFP. The JoongAng Ilbo newspaper reported this week that the foreign ministry requested around $100 million in aid for Ukraine in next year's budget, including $50 million for a NATO trust fund and $20 million in humanitarian assistance. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said in July that the country had pledged $100 million in comprehensive assistance to Ukraine at a NATO summit. results.title: Cheonghae unit to come under on-scene commander's tactical control in limited manner: Seoul
results.content: South Korea's key anti-piracy unit will come under an on-scene commander's tactical control during a multinational security mission under a motion to expand its operational scope, but such authority will be exercised in a "very restricted" manner, Seoul officials said Thursday. The defense ministry submitted to the National Assembly this week a revised motion to expand the operational scope of the Cheonghae Unit from the current zone in waters off the Somali coast to south of Oman in the Arabian Sea, about 650 kilometers away from the Strait of Hormuz. The motion stipulates that the unit will be placed under the "tactical control" of an on-scene commander when it engages in multinational maritime security missions, led by the U.S.-led Combined Maritime Forces (CMF) or the European Union. results.title: N. Korea warns of action against US-led naval buildup
results.content: North Korea on Thursday denounced what it called a U.S.-led naval buildup and nuclear submarine programs, warning it would counter the growing naval threat with unspecified "action." Kim Jong-sik, first vice department director of the Central Committee of the ruling Workers' Party of Korea, made the remarks in a statement carried by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). "Arms build-up of the U.S. and its vassal allies for seizing a maritime edge in the Asia-Pacific region has emerged as a new dangerous factor seriously disturbing regional peace and security," Kim said. He described nuclear submarine programs in South Korea, Japan and Australia as the "detailed implementation" of a new U.S. security strategy aimed at "securing the maritime hegemony." results.title: Foreign correspondents' club in Seoul voices concern over Russia's detention of Japanese journalist
results.content: A foreign correspondents' club based in Seoul on Thursday expressed deep concern over Russia's detention of a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage, stressing that legitimate journalistic activities must be respected. Last month, Russia's Federal Security Service said it had detained a Japanese journalist working for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper in the far eastern Sakhalin region on suspicion of espionage. "Gathering information in the public interest is fundamental to journalism. Legitimate newsgathering and reporting activities must be respected, and any action that threatens a journalist's personal safety on such grounds cannot be justified," the Seoul Foreign Correspondents' Club (SFCC) board said in a statement posted on its website. results.title: ATEEZ enjoy newfound fame in Korea after 'BAD' success: 'People recognize us now'
results.content: K-pop boy group ATEEZ, already a major force on the global music scene, is enjoying a new level of recognition at home following the success of its hit song "BAD" — with members saying even everyday encounters have changed, from receiving extra freebies at shops to being recognized without having to introduce themselves. The eight-member group — Hongjoong, Seonghwa, Yunho, Yeosang, San, Mingi, Wooyoung and Jongho — held a press conference Thursday at Novotel Ambassador in Gangnam, southern Seoul, ahead of the release of its 15th mini-album, "GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6." The album marks ATEEZ's first comeback since "BAD" became a sensation, helping the group expand its popularity among the general public in Korea after years of building a strong international fan base. results.title: Korean won hits 15-day high against US dollar on foreign inflows
results.content: The Korean won extended gains to its strongest level in 15 days against the U.S. dollar Thursday, as foreign investors remained net buyers of local stocks. The won was quoted at 1,330.7 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., up 2.9 won from the close of the previous stock trading session. At one point in afternoon trading, the won rose to a high of 1,327.7 won per dollar, marking the strongest level since Oct. 28. The won's advance was also supported by local exporters' dollar sales. Foreign investors bought a net 340 billion won ($255 million) worth of local shares during the latest regular stock trading session, while the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index dipped 0.61 percent to close at 5,342.73.

results.title: KEPCO Q3 net plunges 78% on higher fuel costs
results.content: The state-run Korea Electric Power Corp. (KEPCO) said Thursday its third-quarter net profit plunged 78 percent from a year earlier due to higher fuel costs. Net profit for the three months ended in September fell to 835.89 billion won from 3.79 trillion won in the same period last year, the company said in a press release. "Electricity sales declined, while global thermal coal prices continued to rise in the third quarter, weighing on our bottom line, among other factors," a company spokesperson said. Combined fuel costs for KEPCO's power-generating subsidiaries, including Korea South-East Power, exceeded 2.2 trillion won in the third quarter, weighing on earnings, the company said. Operating profit plunged 70.9 percent to 1.64 trillion won from 5.65 trillion won during the same period, while sales fell 2.6 percent to 26.85 trillion won from 27.57 trillion won. results.title: Lee says Korean capital market undervalued, urges measures to boost competitiveness
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung said Thursday that Korea's capital market remains undervalued, calling for measures to boost its global competitiveness and attract long-term investments. The president made the remarks at a meeting with his key aides at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul, as Korea's stock market has experienced significant volatility in recent months. After reaching an all-time closing high of 9,114.55 points in late June, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) closed at 5,342.73 points on Thursday, leaving many investors on edge. The president said the country's capital market has been significantly affected by recent external uncertainties. Given the country's economic fundamentals and corporate competitiveness, Korea's capital market "is an attractive investment destination that still remains undervalued," Lee told the meeting. results.title: Korea, Belgium discuss leak of personal data of President Lee, Europe trip entourage
results.content: Korea and Belgium have discussed the leak of personal information belonging to President Lee Jae Myung and members of his entourage during his June trip to Belgium and other parts of Europe, and agreed to maintain close communication on the matter, Seoul's foreign ministry said Thursday. The issue was discussed during a Seoul meeting between First Vice Foreign Minister Park Yoon-joo and Theodora Gentzis, secretary-general of Belgium's foreign ministry, held Friday, according to the ministry. "During the meeting, ways to promote cooperation in various areas were discussed, and the data leak was also discussed," ministry spokesperson Park Doo-soon told a press briefing in response to a reporter's question about possible cooperation between the two countries on the incident. results.title: S. Korea falls to Australia to open regional baseball tournament
results.content: Korea lost to Australia 7-8 in its first game of a regional baseball tournament in Tokyo on Thursday as its comeback effort went for naught. Korea rallied from a 4-0 deficit to take a 6-4 lead, only to give up four runs over the final two innings in the teams' first game of the Asia Professional Baseball Championship (APBC) at Tokyo Dome. This is the third edition of the tournament, which also features the host country Japan and Taiwan. Japan won the first two editions, with Korea finishing as the runner-up on both occasions. The APBC is for players aged 24 years and younger or those with no more than three years of professional experience. Teams can each take up to three players who are between 24 and 29 years old. results.title: [COVER STORY] Korean investors in Nvidia suffer estimated $2.4 bil. in valuation losses
results.content: A deepening scandal involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is unnerving Korean investors, as the chip giant's shares are falling and uncertainty mounts over his future. Nvidia is the second-most-held U.S. stock among Korean investors after Tesla, leaving local shareholders exposed to mounting losses as the chipmaker's shares plunged amid the scandal. Korean investors held about $13.65 billion worth of Nvidia shares as of Thursday, according to data from the Korea Securities Depository. An estimated 800,000 retail investors in Korea own shares in the chipmaker. Nvidia shares have fallen nearly 15 percent since the company announced an investigation into these allegations. results.title: Korean retail investors struggle to cut losses, holding on to or buying more losing stocks
results.content: Two-thirds of Korean retail investors hold on to losing stocks or buy more in an attempt to lower their average purchase price, rather than sell at a loss, a report showed Thursday. The findings are based on an online survey of 1,000 people in their 20s to 50s with experience investing in domestic or overseas stocks, conducted by financial research institute Toss Insight from July 11 to Aug. 21. Of the respondents, 42.2 percent said they continued holding losing stocks, while another 24.4 percent said they bought more shares to bring down their average purchase price. The survey also found that investors who cut their losses according to predetermined rules were less likely to report losses in stocks. results.title: Once a cheap meal, gimbap sees steepest price hike in Seoul
results.content: Gimbap, long considered an affordable meal in Korea, has seen the steepest price increase among popular dining options in Seoul this year, with the average price of a roll approaching 4,000 won ($2.80), up more than 5 percent from the end of last year. According to data released Wednesday by the Korea Consumer Agency's price information portal, Champrice, the average price of a roll of gimbap in Seoul reached 3,923 won in September, up 5.4 percent from 3,723 won in December last year. This was the largest increase among eight popular dining options tracked in Seoul: naengmyeon (cold buckwheat noodles), bibimbap (rice mixed with vegetables), kimchi jjigae (kimchi stew), samgyeopsal (grilled pork belly), jjajangmyeon (noodles in black bean sauce), samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup), kalguksu (hand-cut noodles) and gimbap. results.title: Police seek arrest warrant for father in killing of son's alleged rape victim
results.content: Police sought an arrest warrant Thursday for a 59-year-old man, surnamed Jin, suspected of killing a 15-year-old girl who was the alleged victim in a statutory rape case involving his son, as investigators continued efforts to establish the motive. The Seongbuk Police Station in Seoul requested the warrant on suspicion of murder. Jin was taken into emergency custody at around 1:40 a.m. Wednesday after allegedly stabbing the girl to death at a shared accommodation property in Seongbuk District, northern Seoul. It remains unclear what motivated him to kill her. Police will bring in a criminal profiler to help determine his motive and seek forensic analysis from the National Forensic Service. His son, 20, has been under investigation on suspicion of statutory rape involving the victim in January. results.title: [EXPLAINER] Why Korea's mandatory tender offer plan is drawing global scrutiny
results.content: The proposed revival of Korea's mandatory tender offer system, abolished in 1998 following the Asian financial crisis, has reignited debate nearly three decades later. The idea behind the system is simple: When someone buys a company, smaller shareholders should have a chance to sell their shares at the same price as the company's largest shareholder. Under the bill pending in the National Assembly, a buyer taking control of a company would have to purchase enough shares through a public tender offer to raise its ownership to at least 50 percent plus one share. The goal is to protect minority shareholders, particularly retail investors, who could otherwise miss out on the higher prices paid in corporate takeovers. results.title: Korea Zinc loses court battle over curbs on Young Poong's voting rights
results.content: A court ruled Thursday that a resolution passed at Korea Zinc's annual shareholder meeting last year that restricted the voting rights of Young Poong Corp. and private equity firm MBK Partners Ltd. must be nullified. Young Poong and MBK formed an alliance under an agreement signed in September 2024 to secure management control of Korea Zinc, the world's largest refined zinc smelter. Since then, the two parties have jointly exercised their voting rights, prompting Korea Zinc Chairman Choi Yun-beom to wage a protracted battle to fend off their takeover bid. The Seoul Central District Court ordered Korea Zinc to revoke the resolution adopted at its March 2025 shareholder meeting in a lawsuit filed by the Young Poong-MBK alliance. results.title: Seoul shares snap 2-day rally amid escalating Nvidia risks
results.content: Korean stocks fell 0.6 percent Thursday to end their two-day rally, weighed heavily down by Nvidia's leadership risks. The local currency was trading higher against the U.S. dollar. The benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) closed down 32.63 points, or 0.61 percent, at 5,342.73, reversing from a 4.39 percent rise on Tuesday and a 2.6 percent gain on Wednesday. Investor sentiment was largely affected by Huang's future as the U.S. chip giant is in close business ties with Korean tech companies. results.content: Major tech-intensive firms here are stepping up internal security training and vigilance against industrial espionage, after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made headlines for his reported affair with Alice Huang, who is suspected of being linked to Chinese intelligence. Some companies have reportedly advised workers to take precautions in their daily lives, including avoiding wearing clothing with company logos outside the workplace. results.title: Special counsel raids NEC over fabricated document on security check
results.content: Investigators raided the National Election Commission (NEC) on Thursday over suspicions the election watchdog falsified an official document to exaggerate the security of its computer servers, a special counsel team said. Twenty-five personnel, including two prosecutors, were sent to the NEC headquarters in Gwacheon, just south of Seoul, and two contractors to execute a search and seizure warrant on related charges, according to the team led by independent counsel Lee Tae-han. The allegation dates back to 2023, when a joint security check involving the National Intelligence Service (NIS) and the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) found the NEC had exaggerated the results of its own security inspection amid concerns over the vulnerability of its computer servers to cyberattacks. results.title: Chances of Trump-Kim meeting at APEC grow slim
results.content: A summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong-un appears unlikely at next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gathering in Shenzhen, China, a Cheong Wa Dae official and security analysts said Thursday, despite Trump’s earlier talk of a potential meeting. results.title: Can tougher reappointment rules curb power of Korea's bank holding company chiefs?
results.content: A corporate governance reform package unveiled by the government to boost transparency of CEO succession at financial companies and rein in long-serving chairmen is facing questions over whether it can deliver meaningful change, according to experts Thursday. Their skepticism centers on whether tougher voting requirements will make a difference when incumbent chairmen already enjoy overwhelming shareholder support, and whether independent directors will be able to challenge management in practice. The announcement comes nearly a year after President Lee Jae Myung publicly criticized what he called a “corrupt inner circle” in which a small group of executives takes turns retaining control of financial firms. results.title: Pay rises, tax bites: Korean workers call for income tax reform
results.content: For Lee, a 43-year-old employee at an IT company in Seoul’s Geumcheon District, a bigger paycheck each year has brought little sense of greater financial security. A pay raise initially feels rewarding, he said. But that feeling fades when he checks his pay statement. Taxes and social insurance contributions have also risen, leaving him with less additional take-home pay than expected. “My salary goes up every year, but things still feel tight after paying loan interest, living expenses and my child’s education costs,” Lee said. “A pay raise that merely keeps pace with inflation doesn’t mean we’re better off. Tax thresholds should also reflect rising prices.” His frustration reflects growing calls to overhaul Korea’s income tax system as nominal wage increases fail to deliver greater purchasing power. results.title: City-backed startup summit bolsters Seoul's drive to be global innovation hub
results.content: Seoul’s annual startup summit, Try Everything 2026, generated more than 2,000 investment reviews and doubled face-to-face investor meetings, bolstering the city’s ambitions to rank among the world's top startup hubs. The two-day global startup festival, held Sept. 9-10 at Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), attracted 8,025 participants, including 1,457 visitors from 67 countries, and featured 912 startups, the Seoul Metropolitan Government said Thursday. The number of participants increased 3.8 percent from 7,729 last year, while startup participation rose 4.2 percent from 875 companies. The event recorded 1,141 one-on-one meetings between startups, investors and major corporations, more than twice the 541 meetings held last year. results.title: Korea welcomes record 20 mil. foreign visitors as K-culture fuels tourism boom
results.content: Korea has crossed a milestone that once seemed distant, welcoming more than 20 million foreign tourists in a single year for the first time as the global popularity of Korean culture fuels demand for travel to the country. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism announced that international arrivals surpassed the 20 million mark on Thursday, just 14 years after Korea first recorded 10 million annual visitors in 2012. The achievement marks a new high for the country's tourism industry, with arrivals expected to continue setting records through the end of the year. The surge has also translated into higher spending and more visitors entering through regional gateways, extending tourism's economic benefits beyond the capital. results.title: SSG Landers sign ex-MLB pitcher Richardson
results.content: The SSG Landers announced their signing of former major league pitcher Lyon Richardson on Thursday. The Landers said Richardson, 26, agreed to a one-year contract worth $1 million, which includes a signing bonus of $100,000. The American right-hander will join the returning ace Pedro Avila at the top of the Landers' rotation next season. Korea Baseball Organization (KBO) clubs are each allowed to sign a maximum two foreign pitchers. They may also sign one Asian quota player each, with most teams filling that spot with a pitcher. Richardson was a second-round pick by the Cincinnati Reds at the 2018 Major League Baseball (MLB) draft.
